turns.speaker: host
turns.text: I use AI to get me off my computer, not on my computer. And so the fact that you were at the gym, got asked to do something, and your disability would be like, yep, go for it, get it done, and finish your workout, it's like a much nicer way to work.
turns.zh: 我用 AI，是为了让自己离开电脑，而不是更离不开电脑。所以你人在健身房，有人找你干个活，你的机器人就会说：好，交给我，马上搞定，你接着练你的。这种工作方式舒服太多了。

turns.speaker: john
turns.text: I was able to just screenshot in Figma these two separate art boards of work that was already in progress. And doing so, I just pointed to those. Had the bot do its work, I didn't even read most of this stuff, it produced three outputs, copy pasted what Ben had sent me on Slack, and said, I think we got all these covered. While I'm on this call, work is getting done, which I really love. I think the fact that I don't have to do this stuff myself is a godsend.
turns.zh: 我只是在 Figma 里截了两个画板的图，都是已经在做的工作，然后把机器人指向它们，让它去干活。它产出的大部分东西我甚至都没细看，它给了三个方案，我把 Ben 在 Slack 上发给我的内容复制粘贴过去，说：我觉得这些都搞定了。我在开这个会的同时，活也在被干完，我真的很喜欢这一点。这些事不用我亲自动手，简直是天赐的礼物。

turns.speaker: peng
turns.text: Now when I go somewhere, I can basically just send Grokbot a photo, a screenshot, or literally just the name of the place, and then figure out what the place is, it'll look it up through Google Places API, and I get the right location, it coordinates, it'll fix the perspective and remove people, and turn it into like a 3D miniature visual style that I used on the site.
turns.zh: 现在我去一个地方，基本上只要给 Grok Bot 发一张照片、一张截图，或者干脆只发个地名，它就会弄清楚这是哪儿，通过 Google Places API 查到正确的位置和坐标，然后校正透视、去掉路人，把它变成我网站上用的那种 3D 微缩风格的画面。

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: AI can feel like a threat to the creative arts. Like look, your highest calling was never to design gradient fills in Figma. And what I tell people is, welcome back to How I AI. I'm Claire Vo, product leader and AI obsessive, here on a mission to help you build better with these new tools. Today I have John and Peng from the Grokbot design team, and they're gonna show us two really awesome AI design use cases. One, how to build a beautiful custom and easy to update personal site that meets the bar of a designer, and two, how Grokbot was used to design. Grokbot, including where Figma Bro can make your life at the gym and work a lot easier.
turns.zh: AI 可能会让人觉得是对创意行业的威胁。我常跟大家说：你看，你人生的最高使命从来就不是在 Figma 里画渐变填充。欢迎回到 How I AI。我是 Claire Vo，产品负责人，也是 AI 重度爱好者，我的使命是帮你用好这些新工具，做出更好的东西。今天请到了 Grok Bot 设计团队的 John 和 Peng，他们会给我们展示两个非常棒的 AI 设计用例。第一，怎么搭建一个漂亮、定制、又容易更新的个人网站，而且能过设计师自己那一关；第二，Grok Bot 是怎么被用来设计 Grok Bot 本身的，包括 Figma Bro 如何让你在健身房和工作中都轻松很多。

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Let's get to it.
turns.zh: 我们开始吧。

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Peng, John, thank you for joining How I AI today.
turns.zh: Peng、John，感谢你们今天来到 How I AI。

turns.speaker: john
turns.text: Glad to be here.
turns.zh: 很高兴来这里。

turns.speaker: peng
turns.text: Happy to share.
turns.zh: 很乐意分享。

turns.speaker: john
turns.text: Thanks for having us.
turns.zh: 谢谢邀请。

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: So I am a big bot girl. Actually, we were just talking before the show last night. We did a Ladies Who Grokbot Night at Andreessen Horowitz. There were 900 registrants align around the block. Grokbot is having its moment. And one of the things I love is so many people inside SpaceX AI actually sharing really practical and unique use cases of how they themselves have found new ways to get work done, build software, do awesome things with Grokbot. So how has it been the past couple of weeks just being in the middle of this sort of explosion in Grokbot interest? How does that feel shipping a product like that?
turns.zh: 我可是 Grok Bot 的铁杆粉丝。其实我们录节目前还在聊，昨晚我们在 Andreessen Horowitz 办了一场 Ladies Who Grokbot 之夜，有 900 人报名，排队排到了街角。Grok Bot 正迎来属于它的高光时刻。我特别喜欢的一点是，SpaceXAI 内部有很多人在分享非常实用又独特的用例，讲他们自己是怎么用 Grok Bot 找到新方法来完成工作、开发软件、做各种很酷的事情。那么过去这几周，身处这波 Grok Bot 热潮的中心，感觉怎么样？发布这样一款产品是什么感受？

turns.speaker: john
turns.text: It's really exciting. I mean, I feel like it's rare to have this amount of attention and this amount of engagement on something that a designer gets to work on. And I think we're learning day by day also from our users. I think there's a lot of questions being asked about us as though we're experts on the product just because we're designing it. But I think we're learning just as much from the users, from people sharing their own workflows, their tips and tricks, especially on X recently, and from you as well, Claire. It's been really fun.
turns.zh: 真的很兴奋。我觉得设计师做的东西能获得这么多关注和参与，是很少见的。而且我们也在每天向用户学习。很多人来问我们问题，好像我们因为设计了这个产品就是专家一样。但其实我们从用户那里学到的一样多，大家会分享自己的工作流、技巧和窍门，最近在 X 上尤其多，也包括从你这里学到的，Claire。整个过程特别有意思。

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: People don't know this, but before we started recording, we were actually scrolling through and prepping screen shares. And as we were going, all of us were like, oh, we need that feature. We need this feature. We need to make this a little bit easier. So it's fun to be able to see the process of this product evolve as it has tremendous product market fit right out the gate. Well, Peng, I know that you have a workflow that you wanna show us. And one of the things I love about Grokbot and AI agents in general, is it's just really opening up new ways to do old things and easier ways to do things that we all used to do before. So walk us through what you're gonna show us and why you think Grokbot is the right way to take on this task.
turns.zh: 大家可能不知道，我们开始录之前，其实在一边翻看一边准备屏幕共享。过程中我们几个都在说：哎，我们需要那个功能，还需要这个功能，这里得再做得简单一点。所以能看到这个产品一边演进、一边一上来就有极强的产品市场契合度，真的很有意思。好，Peng，我知道你有一个工作流要给我们展示。我很喜欢 Grok Bot，以及整体上 AI 智能体的一点，就是它们为老事情打开了新做法，让我们以前做的那些事变得更简单。给我们讲讲你要展示什么，以及为什么你觉得 Grok Bot 是完成这件事的合适方式。

turns.speaker: peng
turns.text: Yeah, so I have this pretty personal story. I eat a lot of Chinese food. And then sometimes when you get a takeout, the rice comes with this white paper box. So there's a red Chinese temple on it. And then last weekend I was looking at it and I had this random thought like, where is this temple? Like, is it a real place? Where is it? So I searched online and I found it might be somewhere in San Francisco Chinatown. And I was like, okay, let's find it out. Like I went to Chinatown. I worked around for a while and I did not actually find the temple, but I took a bunch of photos along the way. And there was this little produce shop about setting fruits and other stuff. And I don't took a photo of it.
turns.zh: 好，我有一个挺私人的故事。我经常吃中餐，有时候叫外卖，米饭会装在那种白色纸盒里，盒子上印着一座红色的中式庙宇。上周末我盯着它看，突然冒出一个念头：这座庙在哪儿？是真实存在的地方吗？我上网搜了一下，发现它可能在旧金山唐人街的某个地方。我就想，好，去找找看。我去了唐人街，转了好一阵，最后其实没找到那座庙，但一路上拍了不少照片。其中有一家卖水果和杂货的小店，我就拍了一张。

turns.speaker: peng
turns.text: And later I was waiting for bus and I used AI to turn it into a 3D clay miniature. And I thought it looked pretty cool. And then later that day when I went back home, I plan to redo my personal website. I procrastinate for that for a while. And then I took that 3D grocery store and then I put it, drop it onto the homepage. So it's a little bit of whimsical, it's fun. The page is super minimal. Basically, it was just this tiny store and then some text about me. At the end, I wrote something like, last scene at JBC Market in Chinatown. And I was like, oh, this was actually kind of interesting 'cause I've always had this problem with personal website that especially as a designer, you spend all this time making one and then you launch it and people look at it for like 30 seconds.
turns.zh: 后来我在等公交的时候，用 AI 把这张照片变成了一个 3D 黏土微缩模型，觉得挺酷的。那天晚些时候回到家，我正打算重做我的个人网站，这事我已经拖了很久。我就把那个 3D 杂货店直接放到了首页上。有点奇趣，挺好玩的。页面极其简洁，基本上就是这家小店，加上几句关于我的介绍。最后我写了一句类似「最近一次出没：唐人街 JBC Market」的话。然后我就想，这其实还挺有意思的，因为个人网站一直有个问题，尤其作为设计师，你花了大把时间做一个，上线之后，别人大概就看个 30 秒。

turns.speaker: peng
turns.text: And then they leave. And honestly, even myself don't really go back to see it that much. So I didn't wanna make it just another personal website. Sitting there, I want it to be a little bit more alive and actually be more useful to me. 'Cause I'm also kind of person that I try to like check into places and I like this idea of having a record of where I've been, who I was with and like what I was doing. And they're having like so many apps on the market to do this, like every couple of years, there's one new check-in app and then people use it for a while and eventually disappears. So I was like, oh, why don't I make it just my personal website? Why don't I create it myself? And immediately I thought, if I'm going to do it, I don't wanna manually do it every single time.
turns.zh: 然后就走了。说实话，连我自己都不怎么回去看。所以我不想让它只是又一个摆在那里的个人网站，我希望它更鲜活一点，对我自己也真正有用。因为我也是那种喜欢到处打卡的人，我喜欢有一份记录，知道自己去过哪儿、和谁一起、在做什么。市面上做这个的应用太多了，每隔几年就冒出一个新的打卡应用，大家用一阵子，最后它就消失了。所以我想，为什么不直接做在我的个人网站上？为什么不自己来做？紧接着我就想到，如果要做，我可不想每次都手动更新。

turns.speaker: peng
turns.text: Why can't it just update itself when I go somewhere? So that's when I started to talk to Grokbot because normally, even for this like simple small ideas, I'm not sure like what I need. Maybe I need a CMS, I need some kind of admin portal, I need to upload an image somewhere, I need to host the website, deploy it, store the code. And I'm like, I don't wanna build all of that. I don't even know like where we're getting started. So I just wanna test it, how it works with Grokbot. I basically told Grokbot here is the idea, what's the simplest way to do it? How can we make this work? And we just started building it. There's no Figma file, there's no SPAC.
turns.zh: 为什么不能我去了哪儿，它就自己更新呢？于是我开始跟 Grok Bot 聊。因为平时哪怕是这么简单的小点子，我都不太确定自己需要什么。也许需要一个 CMS，需要某种管理后台，需要把图片传到某个地方，需要托管网站、部署、存代码。我心想，这些我都不想搭，我甚至不知道该从哪儿下手。所以我就想试试用 Grok Bot 会怎么样。我基本上就是告诉 Grok Bot：我的想法是这样的，最简单的做法是什么？怎么才能跑通？然后我们就开始动手做了。没有 Figma 文件，也没有需求文档。

turns.speaker: peng
turns.text: Honestly, I didn't really know where it was going. I was just trying to build one thing and then look at it and then think about, oh, well, what if it can do this? What if it can do that? And then implement it and then we get another idea. So it's very fun just to going with the flow and like trust the vibe. And eventually this idea turned into a checking pipeline. So now when I go somewhere, I can basically just send Grokbot a photo, a screenshot, or literally just the name of the place. And I'll figure out what the place is, it'll look it up through Google Places API and I get the right location, it coordinates, it will process the image, it will generate a light version and a dark version.
turns.zh: 说实话，我自己都不知道它最后会变成什么样。我只是先做出一个东西，看一看，然后想：要是它还能做这个呢？还能做那个呢？然后把它实现，接着又冒出新的点子。就这样顺其自然、相信感觉，特别好玩。最后这个想法变成了一个打卡流程。现在我去一个地方，基本上只要给 Grok Bot 发一张照片、一张截图，或者干脆只发个地名，它就会弄清楚这是哪儿，通过 Google Places API 查到正确的位置和坐标，然后处理图片，生成一个亮色版本和一个暗色版本。

turns.speaker: peng
turns.text: It'll fix the perspective and remove people. I isolate the facade of that building and turn it into like a 3D miniature visual style that I use on the site. And then I was like, okay, location is one thing, but a lot of time, more interesting part is the people, like who am I with? So I added that too.
turns.zh: 它会校正透视、去掉路人，把那栋建筑的立面单独抠出来，变成我网站上用的那种 3D 微缩风格。然后我又想，地点只是一方面，很多时候更有意思的是人，比如我跟谁在一起。所以我把这个也加上了。

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: I was gonna say, that looks like Twin Peaks. I was like, is it Twin Peaks? Did I get it right? It looks great.
turns.zh: 我正想说，那看起来像双子峰。是双子峰吗？我猜对了吗？看起来很棒。

turns.speaker: peng
turns.text: Yeah, that was three days ago. So now when I hand out with a friend, I can literally send a screenshot of the place and a screenshot of my friend's social profile and the Grok bot will take over the rest. So I have this checking bot that I specifically built for this workflow. It figures everything out, it turns it into a data structure that my website expect. Maybe we can try it now. Like if three of us meet in a physical place, maybe a famous landmark or something, we can name a place.
turns.zh: 对，那是三天前。所以现在我跟朋友出去玩，只要发一张地点的截图，再发一张朋友社交主页的截图，剩下的就全交给 Grok Bot 了。我专门为这个工作流做了一个打卡机器人，它会把一切都搞清楚，整理成我网站需要的数据结构。要不我们现在就试试？假设我们三个在某个实际地点碰面，比如某个著名地标之类的，我们可以说个地名。

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Oh, I'll name, 'cause I live in Bernal Heights. So why don't you say we're at Bernal Heights, I guess just called Bernal Heights Peak.
turns.zh: 哦，我来说一个，因为我住在 Bernal Heights。不如就说我们在 Bernal Heights，我猜那里就叫 Bernal Heights Peak。

turns.speaker: peng
turns.text: Either like a specific building or like a landmark.
turns.zh: 可以是一栋具体的建筑，也可以是一个地标。

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Yeah, it's kind of like Twin Peaks. It's just a different, it's another hill in San Francisco.
turns.zh: 对，它有点像双子峰，只是不同的一座，是旧金山的另一座小山。

turns.speaker: peng
turns.text: Okay, since we are not there, but we can just find it.
turns.zh: 好，虽然我们不在那儿，但可以直接找一下。

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Oh, at the swing, there is a clandestine swing. You see it right here? Yep, that's it. That somebody keeps putting up and the city keeps pulling down. Very, it's like a real point of contention.
turns.zh: 哦，就在那个秋千那儿，那里有个私自挂上去的秋千。你看到了吗，就在这儿？对，就是它。总有人把它挂上去，市政府又一直把它拆下来，算是个挺有争议的地方。

turns.speaker: peng
turns.text: Okay, let's see if it works. And I'll put your social handle and John's social handle there.
turns.zh: 好，看看能不能成。我把你的社交账号和 John 的社交账号也放进去。

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: I love this pipeline. I have to take a step back while you're getting this to load. So I think the hardest thing for AI to do is build a personal site that a designer will like about themselves. So just the fact that you were able to get to that point, I mean, I've been a designer in a past life. I just avoid my personal site because I hate the idea of deciding something represents me and shipping it. So the fact that even you could get to something you like, I'm very impressed with. And then the second thing that I think is so fun is you've made it really easy and low friction for you to keep the site updated in a really unique, high quality visual way.
turns.zh: 我太喜欢这个流程了。趁它加载的时候，我得退一步说两句。我觉得对 AI 来说最难的事情，就是做出一个让设计师本人满意的个人网站。你能做到这一步就已经很厉害了。我以前也当过设计师，我一直在逃避做个人网站，因为我很讨厌去决定某个东西能代表我，然后把它发布出去。所以连你都能做出一个自己满意的东西，我非常佩服。第二点我觉得特别好玩的是，你让更新网站这件事变得非常简单、几乎没有阻力，而且还是用一种很独特、很高质量的视觉方式。

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: So I think that is really interesting. If you had to go home and download your photo and copy and paste in the X profiles and do all this stuff, you probably wouldn't keep the site updated. It's too much mental load. And so I love this idea that you've compressed all of these steps that you would have had to do, I mean, historically probably through some sort of CMS or pushing directly to the site to just a bot that has a very specific use case and does this for you. I'm curious while this is running, how did you get it to generate these 3D images so well and so high quality?
turns.zh: 这一点我觉得很有意思。如果你得回家下载照片、把 X 主页复制粘贴进去、再做一堆别的事，你大概根本不会坚持更新网站，心智负担太重了。所以我很喜欢这个思路：你把原本必须做的所有步骤，过去大概得通过某种 CMS 或直接推送到网站来完成，全都压缩成了一个用途非常明确、替你搞定这件事的机器人。趁它还在跑，我很好奇，你是怎么让它把这些 3D 图生成得这么好、质量这么高的？

turns.speaker: peng
turns.text: Yeah, so the pipeline behind it is like figured out by Grokbot. It would generate two images, one light, one dark, 'cause when a theme turns too dark, I want the lights to turn on. I wanted two versions of the image. And then they have to be consistent and then this was baked in the prompt. And I think the interesting part for me is none of this is actually fancy. It's just a bunch of pretty simple building blocks. There's Google Places or Google Maps and then there's image generation and there's some structured data and then there's the website, just render everything. And then Grokbot is basically the thing that connects all the dots together. And I think that felt a little bit different to me because before I would have probably had this idea, I thought about all the stuff I need to do and maybe do it later and I'll never do it.

turns.zh: 我必须说，看，那里出现了 Tradbot，Claire 的个人机器人，非常非常受欢迎，真的改变了我的生活。我喜欢这个，因为这些东西太漂亮了。作为设计师，你想把时间花在把这些素材做得真正出色上，并不一定要去做制作类设计，也就是把它延展到各种不同的素材上、打磨各种版本。所以我猜，你能把更多时间花在那些让这个系统真正可扩展的基础上，然后让 Figma Bro，我超爱这个名字，顺便说一句，Figma Bro 和 Tradbot 肯定能成为朋友，让 Figma Bro 去做制作的活儿，我觉得真的很棒。

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: And then for folks that missed it, what I tell people is, I use AI to get me off my computer, not on my computer. And so the fact that you were at the gym, got asked to do something, especially something like Figma that really does require your human fingers on a touch pad or whatever to do it, and your disability to be like, yep, go for it, get it done and finish your workout, I think is so nice. It's just like a much nicer way to work.
turns.zh: 对于刚才没听到的朋友，我常跟大家说：我用 AI，是为了让自己离开电脑，而不是更离不开电脑。所以你当时在健身房，被叫去做一件事，尤其是像 Figma 这种真的需要你亲手在触控板之类的东西上操作的活儿，而你能说一句：好，去吧，搞定它，然后继续把训练做完，我觉得太好了。这就是一种舒服得多的工作方式。

turns.speaker: john
turns.text: Yeah, and speaking of on the go, the other bot that I wanna highlight is DevBot or Experiments, both of them I kind of use interchangeably, but the high level idea behind these is a lot of times you get an idea, an interaction or a layout, a specific type of design that you want to explore. But once again, you might not be at your computer, classic shower thoughts moment where you wanna capture something and maybe even get it to a certain level of fidelity, but you don't have the time and energy just then in there to do so. Which brings me to DevBot, who works really closely with Experiments also over here. So, I mean, you're starting to see a pattern in the way that I work. This was also on the go. I took a screenshot of our actual mobile app experience, a screenshot of my bot called Slack Search and gave a voice memo to the bot saying, I wanted to make a specific type of prototype.
turns.zh: 对，说到随时随地，我想重点介绍的另一个机器人是 DevBot，或者叫 Experiments，这两个我基本混着用。它们背后的大思路是：很多时候你会冒出一个想法，比如一个交互、一个布局，或者某种你想探索的特定设计。但同样，你可能不在电脑前，就是经典的洗澡时灵光一现，你想把它记下来，甚至做到一定的保真度，但当时没有时间和精力去做。这就要说到 DevBot 了，它和这边的 Experiments 配合得非常紧密。你应该开始看出我工作方式里的规律了。这个也是在路上做的。我截了一张我们手机 App 实际体验的图，又截了一张我那个叫 Slack Search 的机器人的图，然后给机器人发了一条语音备忘录，说我想做一种特定的原型。

turns.speaker: john
turns.text: So I described it, all using voice, kind of rambling a little bit, but in essence it was, when I share an agent, we've been using this term of a snapshot, a template. It's not the agent itself, but it's a copy of it to give to another coworker or a friend or whatever. And so the idea was, what if it would actually do a screenshot effect? If I click the share button, it takes a screenshot, strings down, zooms back to the preview template. And I just had that idea, wanted to test it, gave it to the bot to run with. And it talked to motion God, because there's a lot of things that I described that were elements on the screen that were transitioning. It had its own conversations. I barely even checked it once again, until I came back to its work. And I'll just jump to the end state, which is right here. We had to recreate some of the components within the test repo that we have, but it came up with two options of what I asked for.
turns.zh: 我全程用语音描述，有点絮絮叨叨的，但本质上是这样：当我分享一个智能体时，我们一直用「快照」或者说「模板」这个说法。它不是智能体本身，而是一份副本，用来给另一位同事或朋友之类的人。所以我的想法是：如果它真的做一个截屏效果会怎样？我点分享按钮，它截一张图，缩小下去，再缩放回预览模板。我只是有了这个想法，想测试一下，就交给机器人去发挥。它还去找了 Motion God 沟通，因为我描述的很多东西都是屏幕上正在过渡的元素。它们自己进行了对话。我同样几乎一次都没去看，直到回来看它的成果。我直接跳到最终状态，就在这里。我们得在现有的测试仓库里重建一些组件，但它针对我的要求给出了两个方案。

turns.speaker: john
turns.text: The first being, if I click share agent here, it has a little screenshot effect, then zooms into it and shows some of the details. I could see the routines of the bot and it moves when I switch tabs, shows the plugins, and then you can copy a link and send it. And I asked for a little bit more of a subtle approach as well. And it basically took that and turned it into a version that just goes directly into the share model. And so clever idea, in the end decided not to go in this direction. I felt a little bit too derivative of kind of the iOS screenshot idea that originated this whole exploration. But I do love how easy it is to take just the concept that normally you would have to either prototype with the noodles and Figma, take the time to actually consider how it gets built if you're prototyping in code, describe it in plain words and say, run with it, do with my description of it how you will interpret it and turn it into something that I can interact with.
turns.zh: 第一个方案是，我在这里点「分享智能体」，它会有一个小小的截屏效果，然后放大进去，展示一些细节。我能看到这个机器人的例行任务，切换标签页的时候它会跟着动，展示插件，然后你可以复制链接发出去。我还要了一个更低调一点的方案，它基本上就是把这个思路改成了一个直接进入分享弹窗的版本。所以是个很聪明的点子，不过最后我们决定不往这个方向走。我觉得它有点太像 iOS 截屏的那种效果了，而整个探索最初正是从那个想法来的。但我真的很喜欢现在这件事有多容易：一个概念，以前你要么得在 Figma 里拉连线做原型，要么如果用代码做原型，就得花时间真正考虑它怎么实现；现在只要用大白话描述出来，说一句：拿去做吧，按你对我描述的理解去做，把它变成我能交互的东西。

turns.speaker: john
turns.text: So ideas bot maybe should be the combination of what I'm using today as experiments and dev bot. But yeah, the random shower thoughts can now become a real working prototype.
turns.zh: 所以「点子机器人」也许应该把我现在用来做实验的那个和 DevBot 合二为一。不过总之，那些洗澡时冒出来的随机想法，现在都能变成真正能用的原型了。

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: One thing that, you know, again, I've been in tech a million years. And so in the past, I am telling you some delightful, amazing designer would have been like, I had this great idea. We're gonna like screen, when we do share the screenshot effect, it's gonna like feel so good. It's gonna like give people a spike of dopamine. They're gonna love it. We're gonna share more things. And what would have happened is you would have hit a product manager that says, not a priority, show me the ROI, what's the OKR? And an engineer being like, I'm not gonna build that stupid thing. I have tech debt to do or like a bunch of stuff. And even if you get through the gauntlet of both of those and you get it built, and you're like, nevermind, don't love it, don't love it. People are angry. They're like, we dedicated time, we prioritize this.
turns.zh: 有件事我得说，我在科技行业待了好多好多年。要是放在以前，我跟你说，某个特别有灵气、特别厉害的设计师会跑来说：我有个好主意，我们做个分享截图的效果，用起来会特别爽，能给人来一下多巴胺，大家会爱死它，会分享更多东西。然后会发生什么呢？你会撞上一个产品经理说：这不是优先级，给我看 ROI，对应哪个 OKR？还会撞上一个工程师说：我才不做这种蠢东西，我还有一堆技术债要还。就算你闯过了这两关、把它做出来了，结果发现：算了，不太喜欢。大家就会很生气：我们投入了时间，我们还专门排了优先级。

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: It's like you don't deprecate any of these things. And so the thing that I call this like the trash can method of software development, which is like building things with the presumption that it is totally inexpensive to throw them in the trash, whether those are prototypes or things that you get to your customers. And I think it allows you to be a lot more expansive about what the process of product development, software development looks like, because you're not always stopping yourself saying, is this enough to justify getting it into the app? Is this enough to bother somebody, to get it higher priority than this or that? And so for somebody who has built a lot of software in a lot of environments for a very long time, that is the piece of products like this that really make me excited, because you can iterate so quickly, you don't have to shut off that like creative part of your brain that says, well, what if this, what if that?
turns.zh: 结果就是这些东西你一个都不会下线。所以我把这个叫作软件开发的「垃圾桶开发法」：做东西的时候就预设把它扔进垃圾桶几乎没有成本，不管是原型，还是已经交到客户手里的东西。我觉得这能让你对产品开发、软件开发的过程放开得多，因为你不用老是拦住自己问：这值得放进应用里吗？值得去打扰别人、把它的优先级排到这个那个前面吗？对一个在各种环境里做了很久很久软件的人来说，这类产品真正让我兴奋的就是这一点：你可以迭代得非常快，不用关掉大脑里那个爱问「要是这样呢、要是那样呢」的创意部分。

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: And you don't have to be stressed that you're quote unquote racing resources. When you come up with an idea that you're not a hundred percent sure of, but wanna see what it looks like.
turns.zh: 而且当你想到一个自己没有百分百把握、但又想看看做出来什么样的点子时，也不用焦虑自己是在「浪费资源」。

turns.speaker: john
turns.text: Totally agree. And I think that makes it more fun to be a designer again, honestly. A lot of the previous constraints, the parts of the design process and working cross-functionally that were a headache before, are a little less of a problem these days, like you said.
turns.zh: 完全同意。说实话，我觉得这让当设计师重新变得好玩了。以前很多限制，设计流程里、跨职能协作里那些让人头疼的部分，就像你说的，现在都没那么成问题了。

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Amazing. Well, I love it just to recap for folks, Figma Bro, your design spotter while you were at the gym, getting the reps in on your art boards, and then experiment in DevBot, basically like take your shower thoughts, take your walk thoughts, and the implementation is none of your business. Let them cook. You come back to an idea and then it's up to you whether or not you wanna ship it or not. Okay, so this has been so fun to recap for folks. We've shown sort of like the personal workflows and how you can do kind of amazing things that you wouldn't have been able to do before with very minimal toil, using GrokBot as sort of like a development and design pipeline. John showed us how to experiment, design, do production more efficiently with GrokBot.
turns.zh: 太棒了。我很喜欢，给大家回顾一下：Figma Bro 是你在健身房时的设计「保护员」，帮你在画板上把次数练够；然后是 DevBot 里的实验，基本上就是把你洗澡时、散步时冒出来的想法交出去，至于怎么实现，那不关你的事，让它们去折腾。你回来就能看到一个成型的点子，要不要上线由你决定。好，给大家回顾这些真的很有意思。我们展示了个人工作流，以及怎么用 Grok Bot 当作一条开发加设计的流水线，几乎不费力气就做出以前做不到的厉害东西。John 给我们展示了怎么用 Grok Bot 更高效地做实验、做设计、做产出。

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Let's just take a step back. Let's go to lightning round questions. My first one, just very quick between you two, other than the bots you showed. I'm like, how do you think about your bots? Who are your favorites? How do you organize them?
turns.zh: 我们稍微退后一步，进入快问快答环节。第一个问题，你们俩快速说一下，除了刚才展示的这些机器人之外，你们怎么看待自己的机器人？最喜欢哪几个？怎么组织它们？

turns.speaker: peng
turns.text: A lot of my digital life has been dedicated to all different types of GrokBots. In general, I organize them in two buckets, life and work. So I have a couple of bots that are dedicated for each part of my life. For example, my chief of staff. I manage all the bots, but I sometimes do talk to other bots, but I delegate the things I don't know who to delegate it to, to the COS bot. So I think last night I was asking it to buy some 3D printing filament for me. So that's the plastic material that 3D printer use to making things. And what's interesting is not only can help you search, find and buy the item, you can actually train different tasks together.
turns.zh: 我数字生活的很大一部分都交给了各种各样的 Grok Bot。总的来说，我把它们分成两类：生活和工作。生活的每个方面都有几个专门的机器人。比如我的幕僚长。所有机器人都由我来管，有时候我也会直接跟其他机器人对话，但遇到不知道该交给谁的事，我就交给这个幕僚长机器人。比如昨晚我让它帮我买一些 3D 打印耗材，就是 3D 打印机用来做东西的那种塑料材料。有意思的是，它不只能帮你搜索、找到并买下东西，你还能把不同的任务串在一起。

turns.speaker: peng
turns.text: Like I asked it once you were done, update the inventory list. 'Cause I keep this 3D printing filament inventory in motion. And I wanted to automatically add this record and purchase it for me. And I think that's truly the power of it is to like train different tasks in our daily life together and then give it like a higher task and let it figure out what the steps, what needs to do, maybe you can learn it. And then the next time you do it, just do the thing that we did last month and then even have it automatically do it. I have an email manager, which will surface all my action items. This was last night I was checking any action items from my input inbox. And then like there was some USPS delivery issue, then I asked it to help me contact them.
turns.zh: 比如我让它买完之后更新库存清单，因为我在 Notion 里记着一份 3D 打印耗材的库存，我希望它自动帮我添加这条记录，并帮我完成购买。我觉得它真正厉害的地方就在这里：把日常生活中不同的任务串起来，然后给它一个更高层的任务，让它自己去想该走哪些步骤、需要做什么，它还能学会。下次你只要说「照上个月那样再做一遍」就行，甚至可以让它自动去做。我还有一个邮件管家，会把我所有的待办事项挑出来。昨晚我就在看收件箱里有没有待办事项，结果有个 USPS 的投递问题，我就让它帮我联系对方。

turns.speaker: peng
turns.text: I have the calendar manager who is effective to become my calendar now. So I'm scheduling someone for a coffee chat next week. And then most of my time today, and I just take a screenshot of the conversation. It can be on any IM tool. This one's on LinkedIn and I just send it and then ask you to put a placeholder on my calendar. Almost never opened the calendar app anymore. You can also put bots into a group. So let's say in this example, I had this idea of designing a app that translated class mail to English. So I throw this idea into the group chat. And then in the group chat, we have a PM, we have a designer, we have a engineer.
turns.zh: 我还有个日历管家，现在它基本上就成了我的日历。比如我要约一个人下周喝咖啡聊聊，我只要把聊天记录截个图，在哪个聊天工具上都行，这次是在 LinkedIn 上，发给它，让它在我日历上先占个位置。我现在几乎不再打开日历应用了。你还可以把机器人拉进一个群里。比如在这个例子里，我有个想法，想设计一个把猫叫声翻译成英文的应用。我把这个想法丢进群聊，群里有一个产品经理、一个设计师、一个工程师。

turns.speaker: peng
turns.text: And then they started to talk about idea from their own perspective. And it's so interesting to see like how this simple seed planted in the group chat and then now like derive new ideas around it. I even use it to prepare the podcast that we're doing right now. I don't have a microphone and I asked my IT bot who's like taking care of all my IT questions. What type of microphone I need? And I only have this one, does it work? And for personal life, it's replacing my news app. So every morning, 7 a.m. I'll receive a newsletter and it's personalized. I tell it, I wanna AI information. I wanna news about AI that relevant to me.
turns.zh: 然后它们就开始从各自的角度讨论这个想法。看着一颗简单的种子种进群聊里，然后围绕它长出新的点子，真的很有意思。我甚至用它来准备我们现在录的这期播客。我没有麦克风，就去问我的 IT 机器人，它负责处理我所有的 IT 问题：我需要什么样的麦克风？我手上只有这一个，能用吗？在个人生活方面，它取代了我的新闻应用。每天早上 7 点我会收到一份个性化的简报。我告诉它，我想要 AI 方面的信息，想要和我相关的 AI 新闻。

turns.speaker: peng
turns.text: I wanted to like have it do fact check and then source the official links as much as possible. And then this one is a legal advisor. So it's taking care of a lot of repetitive tasks. For example, I'm in this wait list for I'm not playing green card. I'm in wait list for this visa bulletin and checking manually every month in a pair. So I just dedicated this task to it. And then I give the link and it will go check it every month. And then let me know, okay, where's the, you are in the queue, what's the waiting list? So data.
turns.zh: 我还让它做事实核查，并且尽量附上官方链接作为来源。还有这个是法律顾问，它帮我处理很多重复性的事情。比如我在申请绿卡，在排签证公告的队，以前每个月都要手动去查，特别麻烦。所以我就把这件事交给了它。我给它一个链接，它每个月都会去查一次，然后告诉我：你现在排到哪了，等候情况怎么样。

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: I love it. So it seems like you have just kind of like all the admin, all the life admin you need to do, whether it's shopping, whether it's checking in on different status, regular check-ins. And then I love the idea of like, I don't want an email anymore and I don't want a calendar anymore. I want a bot to tell me where to show up and that's it. And so just for folks watching this, again, it's like make it as easy as possible to take the task you're doing to the finish line. You knew you needed to buy 3D printing filament, but you just don't want to open up the app, click the buttons, pick the right one, get sucked into the reviews, get distracted by the associated products, you're just like buy the thing.
turns.zh: 我太喜欢了。看起来你基本上把所有的杂务、所有生活琐事都交给它了，不管是购物、查各种状态，还是定期跟进。我也很喜欢这个想法：我不想再看邮件了，也不想再看日历了，我只想让一个机器人告诉我该去哪儿出现，就这样。所以对正在看的各位来说，还是那句话：让你手上的任务尽可能轻松地走到终点。你知道自己得买 3D 打印耗材，但就是不想打开应用、点按钮、挑对型号、被评论区吸进去、又被相关商品分了心，你只想说：把这个东西买了。

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Or even calendar events, you like pull it up and you look and I have a conflict, what do I do? And you get distracted by Slack. Like all these things I think just allow you to kick off a task and pull it all the way through without distraction and just make sure that you get a lot of stuff done. And I think the breadth of use cases here is pretty incredible. John, do you have any that are different than this? Like one or two that you think folks aren't thinking of or that are a little different than the average, you know, admin shopping one?
turns.zh: 日历上的事也一样，你打开一看，发现有冲突，怎么办？然后又被 Slack 分了心。我觉得这些做法能让你把一个任务启动起来，然后一路推到底，不被打断，确保你能搞定一大堆事情。这里的用例覆盖面真的很惊人。John，你有没有跟这些不太一样的？有没有一两个你觉得大家想不到的，或者跟一般的杂务、购物类不太一样的？

turns.speaker: john
turns.text: I do have some that are a little bit particular and one is just, I just started a few days ago. I've been learning Japanese and the thing about Japanese as a language is there's Hiragana, there's Katakana and there's Kanji and so there's different ways of reading one language. And recently I had the thought to just maybe communicate with this bot, which is just a Japanese practice bot, both in a way to up level my reading of Kanji as much as possible, but then have the pronunciation underneath it when I need it as well as finally an English response. So I just basically told it, give me all three forms so that I can learn as I go in just regular communication with you, I was having a look for a specific book as you could tell up above, I was gonna have it translated but then it came out so I ended up buying it.
turns.zh: 我确实有几个比较特别的，其中一个是几天前才刚开始用的。我最近在学日语，日语这门语言的特点是有平假名、片假名，还有汉字，所以同一种语言有好几种读法。最近我想到，可以跟这个机器人交流，它就是一个日语练习机器人，一方面尽可能提升我读汉字的水平，另一方面在我需要的时候在下面标上读音，最后再给一个英文回复。所以我基本上就是告诉它：每次都把这三种形式都给我，这样我在跟你日常交流时就能边用边学。你上面也能看到，我当时在找一本特定的书，本来打算让它帮我翻译，结果那本书出了，我最后就直接买了。
